item.title: ‘We need that’ – LaMelo Ball shares cold reality for Timberwolves after surprising loss to Bulls
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball did not mince his words after the team’s win streak came to an end with a 117-106 loss to the Chicago Bulls. The Timberwolves had done an excellent job of remaining competitive with franchise star Anthony Edwards out with an injury, primarily because of how new star addition Ball has helped the Wolves thrive in this stretch. Unfortunately, Ball’s magic ran out against the lowly Bulls on November 15, but the 25-year-old guard is taking away the perfect lesson after the loss. LaMelo Ball thinks the Timberwolves needed to get their ‘head busted in’ After riding high over a four-game win streak that ended at the hands of one of the perceived weaker teams in the NBA, Ball admitted the Timberwolves needed a loss like this to get themselves back on track. “Yeah, I mean s—, we got out head busted in, so I mean s— we should be ready to play. Yeah, like a little a– whooping by your pops or something, get you back on track. S—, we need that.” Ball stuffed the stat sheet with 19 points, eight rebounds, six assists and four steals in the loss, but it was not enough to stop the Bulls, who took this win buoyed by Norman Powell’s 24 points and Matas Buzelis’ 18 points and nine rebounds. The Timberwolves lost the game on team production and because Chicago caught fire from three (14/30 3PM) . Bench players such as Buddy Hield (16 PTS), Tre Jones (16 PTS) and Patrick Williams (14 PTS) caught fire as well, with the Wolves’ rotation failing to respond. Ball is averaging 18.6 points, 6.2 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.9 steals this season, proving that the Charlotte Hornets might have given up on him too easily. While he’s Minnesota’s No. 1 option right now, he will soon have to readjust to playing alongside Edwards, the true leading offensive option for the franchise. item.title: Bengals vs. Steelers: How to watch, game time, TV info, online stream, and more
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers are setting up for one of the most important games of the week. It will be showcased on Sunday Night Football as these teams fight for first place in the AFC North. The Bengals are coming off handling the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid quite easily. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins continued their dominant offensive march since halftime against the Baltimore Ravens. The defense did enough to keep the Falcons at bay, but part of that was due to Atlanta abandoning the outside running game. The Steelers are coming off their Bye Week. It is kind of funny that the team that played an international game not only doesn’t get their bye week following the trip across the ocean, but their opponent got theirs during the week they were gone. Pittsburgh has shown their defense is their biggest strength, as only three teams have scored more than 20 points against them. One of those teams was the Indianapolis Colts, who kicked five field goals that game. Another was the Bengals themselves. The first game ended with a Burrow fumble as the team was nearly in position for at least a tying field goal. What was more frustrating was the punt unit committing two huge mistakes that resulted in points for Pittsburgh. There was a muffed punt as well as a 15-yard penalty for running into the punter. Those extra possessions resulted in 10 points. We will see if this one plays out differently in the jungle. I feel like this was really big for our spirit.” Akron Beacon Journal sports writer Michael Beaven can be reached by email at mbeaven@thebeaconjournal . Friars defense pays off Hightower's bucket capped a 16-0 run and gave Providence a 14-0 advantage off nine Colorado turnovers. Page occasionally featured at the four alongside Jacob Bannarbie and Samson Aletan at the five, giving the Friars a bigger lineup inside. Elijah Saunders did not play after seeing early time in each of Providence's last two games against the Cornhuskers and Bulldogs. His absence was due to the coach's decision – Devin Vanterpool (right shoulder) was out after suffering a sprain in practice and will be bidding to make his return in time for the Maui Invitational next week. Walters did not play against the Black Bears or Nebraska, but he made an impact against Bryant and logged nearly 19 minutes in this one. His biggest contribution came late, a jumper off an inbounds play in what was a 59-53 game. It was the only time Colorado (2-2) drew within two possessions in the second half, and the Friars (3-1) had missed their previous six shots from the floor. That's something we work on every day in practice." Walters tallied six points and three rebounds while closing with a plus-12 rating. Hightower was the only better Providence player in that category, finishing at plus-18. Walters took stretch minutes from Mela and Leonardo Marangon, thanks to putting the everyday work he's done in practice on display here. item.title: Middlesbrough rule out January sale of 15-goal striker Will Lankshear despite growing interest from Arsenal, Tottenham and Manchester United
item.description: Bolton Wanderers v Middlesbrough - Sky Bet Championship 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Middlesbrough have ruled out selling prolific striker Will Lankshear during the January transfer window despite mounting interest from Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester United. The 21-year-old has scored 15 goals in 16 appearances across all competitions since arriving on Teesside in a deal worth up to £20 million. Teesside chiefs reject winter exit According to TEAMtalk , Boro are dismissive of any suggestion they could be convinced to cash in on Lankshear mid-season while chasing top-flight promotion. Under contract at the Riverside Stadium until June 2031, the Championship's leading marksman has netted 13 goals in 13 league games alongside two goals across three Carabao Cup outings. Insiders indicate the youngster is thoroughly enjoying life in the North East and wants to stay. Premier League heavyweights monitor marksman Having watched the frontman flourish since his move from north London, the majority of top-flight clubs have sent scouts to monitor his progress this term. The report states that former employers Spurs are keeping close tabs on his development and have not ruled out a future approach, even though they only inserted a matching-right option rather than a formal buy-back clause into the transfer agreement. Boyhood club Arsenal are also tracking their former academy prospect alongside top-flight rivals United, Brighton & Hove Albion and Everton, while regional neighbours Newcastle United, Sunderland and Leeds United have checked on his displays. Beyond domestic admirers, Bundesliga heavyweights Borussia Dortmund have utilised their extensive English scouting network to watch the marksman, though no suitor has made formal contact with Boro or the player's camp. Hamstring setback delays England call-up With the Championship outfit unwilling to entertain winter bids and the striker settled on Teesside, a New Year switch is considered unrealistic despite his prolific strike rate. Instead, his ruthless penalty-box displays have brought him to the brink of senior international honours. Former Three Lions striker Michael Owen previously urged national team boss Thomas Tuchel to consider the Boro talisman earlier this season. In fact, the forward was pencilled in to feature in the senior England squad for this month's Nations League clashes against Croatia and Spain before a minor hamstring problem ruled him out of contention. Promotion chasers prepare for return That muscle issue also sidelined Lankshear for his club's recent goalless draws against Wrexham and Watford, though the problem is not deemed serious. Middlesbrough currently sit second in the Championship standings on 29 points, level with leaders Birmingham City and third-placed Stoke City. They resume their promotion push following the international break when they host Bristol City in Matchday 16 on Saturday, November 21.

item.title: Josh Hokit and Alex Pereira bury the hatchet in backstage conversation at UFC 334
item.description: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC Alex Pereira thinks Josh Hokit beat Ciryl Gane at UFC 334. ‘Poatan’ let his rival know that opinion when they crossed paths backstage at Madison Square Garden on Saturday night. The headliner in New York City saw Gane successfully defend his undisputed heavyweight title for the first time a couple of months after Tom Aspinall vacated the throne. France’s top MMA star beat Hokit via unanimous decision following five rounds of action, but Pereira disagreed with the judges’ scorecards. Alex Pereira congratulates Josh Hokit on his UFC 334 performance Hokit has become known for his controversial gimmick and trash talk, something ‘The Incredible Hok’ did not let up ahead of his first title shot at UFC 334. Arguably the man targeted the most by the American’s schtick has been Pereira. But despite their history this year, the Brazilian had nothing but good things to say to Hokit. Cameras caught the pair running into each other backstage at MSG after Hokit’s hard battle with ‘Bon Gamin’. While they had to be separated during an encounter earlier this year in Washington, DC, the interaction on November 14 played out very differently. “Hey bro, chama. Congrats, my brother. For me, you won,” Pereira said after shaking hands with Hokit. The polarizing American heavyweight returned that respect by wishing ‘Poatan’ luck in his fight against Sergei Pavlovich next month. The result of Pereira’s UFC 335 co-main event could either set up a rematch with Gane or a clash with Hokit, which Dana White described as “fun” during his post-event press conference on Saturday. After title wins at light heavyweight and middleweight, Pereira is still chasing a historic third belt, having missed out on the achievement in his heavyweight debut against Gane this past June. item.description: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin. © Reuters Connect Lane Kiffin has been one of college football’s most hated personalities since joining LSU. Now, he may have given his detractors even more ammunition. On Saturday, the head coach’s LSU lost 21-22 to Texas despite leading 21-10 in the third quarter and nabbing three interceptions on Arch Manning. The pivotal moment came when the quarterback found running back Raleek Brown for a touchdown catch with just three seconds left: That loss eliminated the Tigers from CFP contention in Kiffin’s first year in charge, and fans took the opportunity to maliciously revel in the result: Despite Manning’s woes, Sam Leavitt proved no better, throwing three interceptions himself. He did, however, throw twice as many touchdowns, with both going to Jackson Harris. Both sides also had a rushing touchdown each, courtesy of Manning for Texas and Dilin Jones for LSU. Lane Kiffin’s handshake with Steve Sarkisian draws poignant response from Kirk Herbstreit Immediately after the game’s final second ticked away, Lane Kiffin was seen shaking hands with Steve Sarkisian . Given the animosity between the two over the transfer portal, it was a surprising moment. item.title: Thomas Tuchel fumes over ‘twisted’ comments on anti-racism protocol before Spain v England
item.description: England head coach Thomas Tuchel stressed that he does not expect any racism in Madrid having been angered before the Spain match by his remarks about protocols being “twisted”. Sunday’s Nations League Group A3 decider is England’s first in the Spanish capital since a friendly in November 2004, when Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips were subject to racist chanting from sections of the home crowd. In addition, Spain must play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity after supporters sang a discriminatory chant about Muslims in March’s game with Egypt. Tuchel stressed in the build-up that he did not expect there to be any racist abuse but added “maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent (in Madrid)”. Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente was asked about the England boss’ comments and said: “I can say the opposite. “Tell Thomas there is no racism. As clear as that. Exactly the same as in England. We’re not racists, none of us.” De la Fuente’s answer was relayed to Tuchel in the pre-match press conference at the Metropolitano, where the England boss admits he “got a bit upset”. item.title: Falcons player fined for actions vs. Bengals
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Falcons in Spain in Week 9 and have turned all their attention to the huge AFC North matchup at Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both teams come into Week 10 with 6-2 records, and the winner of this weekend’s game will have the inside track to hosting a playoff game and could push for a first-round bye. The league, though, is still dotting the i’s and crossing the t’s from Week 9, and in doing so, they found it necessary to fine Falcons wide receiver Drake London for lowering his helmet and using it as a battering ram against Bengals cornerback DJ Turner. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the league fined London $23,882 for use of helmet on the final play of the third quarter. It’s not often offensive players get fined in the NFL, but when ball carriers lower their helmets to gain a few extra yards, they put their own health and the health of the defender in jeopardy. Luckily, both Turner and London walked away from this one without a scratch. item.title: Kentucky rushes for season-low in disappointing loss to Florida
item.description: Kentucky hosted the Florida Gators as its final night game of the 2026 season at Kroger Field. It was a weird, back-and-forth game in which Florida left with a win. The game was full of storylines, with transfers on both sides, but primarily involving the coaches on the Gators’ sideline. Jon Sumrall, former player and coach at Kentucky, would return to his old Kentucky home for the first time since his departure in 2022 to be the head coach at Troy. Another coach over on that sideline was Kentucky’s defensive coordinator under Mark Stoops for the final six years of his tenure in Lexington. No doubt those two would want to go back to Gainesville with a win, with both having a chip on their shoulder heading into the contest. Well, the two defensive-minded coaches got to leave with smiles on their faces after a 21-14 victory for Florida. How did they do it? Well, they stopped the run. Kentucky came into the night averaging 163.7 yards on the ground per game, and left tonight’s contest with only 61 yards. Start to finish, the Florida defense never let Kentucky get rolling at all. The offense tried everything they could to get something going, from throwing different players out there to different formations and motions, but nothing helped. Florida came in with a plan to stop Kentucky on the ground, and they executed it. CJ Baxter, Jason Patterson, Jovantae Barnes, Mikkel Skinner, Brennen Ward, and Kenny Minchey all had their chances to run the ball, and none could break through. In all honesty, Minchey may have looked the best, even though he only ended the game with one yard due to sack yards. “Didn’t establish the run tonight, at all,” Stein said about the struggling run game. “Got out-physicalled at the point of attack. That, to me, was the early indication: not being able to run the ball; you run it for 61 yards on 27 carries. And they rush it for 211 on 48; that’s a problem. We’ve gotta address it and get it fixed.” Kentucky won’t have a chance at the dream season we had all started to believe in with them dropping out of the College Football Playoff, but there’s still pride to play for, as Stein and multiple players said. Running the ball for over 100 fewer yards will help you end the season with four straight losses if you’re not careful. With a road game to Missouri on deck and a home game against Louisville following it, Kentucky’s offense has got to figure some things out in the run game. It was unacceptable against Florida and is certainly one of the more eye-opening stats when you look at how Kentucky defeated Florida.

Iyer also pointed out that India does not get centre-wicket practice during overseas assignments. Shreyas Iyer says New Zealand series win cannot be compared directly to the 2027 ODI World Cup India's stand-in captain for the last two ODIs against New Zealand, Shreyas Iyer, has offered a different perspective on India's 2027 ODI World Cup preparations, after the team's permanent captain, Shubman Gill, previously identified the ongoing New Zealand series as an important opportunity for the team ahead of next year's tournament. India clinched the five-match ODI series 3-1 after defeating New Zealand by 22 runs in the final match at Bay Oval on Sunday. item.title: Newark Catholic graduate Wright coaches Otterbein to OAC record
item.description: WESTERVILLE - The Otterbein volleyball team stands above the rest in the history of the Ohio Athletic Conference. Otterbein swept visiting Muskingum, 25-22, 25-10, 25-17, on Nov. 14 to win an OAC-record fifth consecutive tournament championship. The Cardinals have been coached throughout their run by Newark Catholic graduate Monica (McDonald) Wright. "Otterbein has been very good to me, and we have had tons of great girls come through the program," said Wright, who has led the Cardinals for two dominant decades shortly after starring as a player at Wittenberg. "We are in an awesome spot where we have six seniors still with the program. When you have that much experience on the floor and the tradition here - I am just super proud of them." Watkins Memorial graduate Elise Adelman piled up 32 assists and added eight kills and nine digs for Otterbein in the championship match. Adelman has played for the Cardinals the past two seasons after setting multiple program records during two seasons at Bloomsburg. "This team is something special. We've had a great season, and we are not done yet. We knew we had to battle, and we did just that," Adelman said. "As soon as I came here, something in me changed. This program, it's a family. I am so happy to be here." Lexi Scott, a Zane Trace graduate, led a a balanced attack with 12 kills to take tournament Most Outstanding Player honors. She, Adelman and Emerson Baum represented Otterbein on the all-tournament team. NC graduate Sydney Gummer totaled four kills and two assisted blocks. Gummer, who has had a standout freshman season after helping the Green Wave win the Division VI state championship a year ago, led the Muskies with 16 kills in their semifinal victory against Mount Union. Sheridan graduate Alexis Bradley, the Muskies’ setter, joined teammate Mackenzie Krous on the all-tournament team. Otterbein this week will continue their impressive season in the NCAA tournament. The Cardinals have qualified for the postseason for the 12th time in 19 seasons under Wright. "(Wright) expects the best from me every day," Adelman said. "She pushes me every day. She knows I can only get better." ksnyder@newarkadvocate.com 740-973-4541 Instagram: @newarkurt This article originally appeared on Newark Advocate: Newark Catholic graduate Wright coaches Otterbein to OAC record

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo tribute party hilariously ruined with help of Newcastle United star
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo shirts The Cristiano Ronaldo tribute party hilariously ended in disaster. The Estádio Municipal de Braga hosting what was intended to be a celebration of the selfish prima donna’s international career. It had always been about Cristiano Ronaldo rather than the team. The 41-year-old embarrassingly walked out of the Portugal camp in September after he was told he would not start the in the Nations League away match against Denmark. Cristiano Ronaldo was given a token £215 fine and 30-day suspension by Portugal. Fast forward less than two months later and ahead of the reverse fixture with Denmark, he was at it again. Rather than doing things properly, Cristiano Ronaldo retired from international football via a video he posted on his social media last week. No advance warning given and Portugal coach Jorge Jesus later revealed that Ronaldo would have been picked for these Uefa Nations League games against Denmark and Wales in November. With his out of the blue announcement, Portugal then quickly made this Saturday night Portugal v Denmark match all about Cristiano Ronaldo. All of the Portugal players and the mascots walked out wearing a ‘Ronaldo 7’ shirt. The fans displayed the word ‘Ronaldo’ in the top tier of one of the stands. The letters ‘GOAT’ on the bottom tier. A banner that translated as ‘thank you, captain’, plus a similar message appearing on the scoreboard in the seventh minute. How brilliant it was then that this all ended in disaster. Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg scored a penalty just before half-time, then Rasmus Hojlund scored twice in eight minutes to make it 3-0 with more than half an hour remaining. With 73 minutes on the clock Newcastle United striker William Osula came off the bench and within a minute had won a free-kick towards the right wing. The resultant free-kick seeing Joachim Andersen head the fourth and the Cristano Ronaldo fan club left in tears as his tribute well and truly had fallen apart. item.title: ’Simply to get a…’- NFL’s latest Drake London fine sparks blunt response from J.J. Watt
item.description: Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images J.J. Watt has questioned the NFL after Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London was handed another hefty fine for unnecessary roughness, with the former defensive end suggesting the league may be trying to provoke a reaction. London was fined $23,882 for using his helmet against Cincinnati Bengals cornerback DJ Turner II during the Falcons’ Week 9 game in Madrid. The latest punishment comes after London was already fined $12,537 for an incident involving Tampa Bay Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone. Both violations were first-time offences in their respective categories. J.J. Watt questions NFL’s decision to fine Drake London again Watt did not hold back when reacting to the latest punishment on X, resharing NFL insider Tom Pelissero’s report. “They have to be doing this simply to get a reaction out of people sometimes… It worked. Twenty. Three. Thousand. Dollars. For this?” Watt posted. The incident occurred with seconds remaining in the third quarter against Cincinnati. After making a 21-yard reception, London lowered his head as he collided with Turner, resulting in the unnecessary roughness penalty. The two fines have now made for an expensive stretch for the Falcons receiver. According to the NFL’s rules, another helmet-related unnecessary roughness violation would see his fine increase to $47,762. London is also tied for the largest fine handed out in Week 9, alongside Seattle Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones, who received the same $23,882 punishment. It has been a difficult campaign for the 24-year-old, who has recorded 44 catches for 692 receiving yards and one touchdown. Atlanta have also struggled, sitting at 3-6 despite London signing a contract extension that keeps him with the franchise through the 2030 season. His disciplinary issues have extended beyond the two fines, too. Earlier in the campaign, London was involved in an exchange with a fan during the Carolina Panthers game, admitting afterwards that he needed to take responsibility for his response. “I’m going to be honest here, I don’t take light to disrespect at all,” London said. “I don’t care who you are. I’m a man, too, at the end of the day. So, if you want to get on a personal level, I can get there, too, but it’s not the right thing to do. So, I got to take accountability for that, and I got to push forward and be the bigger man in some of those situations.” The NFL distributes fine money equally between NFLPA retired player support programmes, the NFL Foundation and other non-profit organisations supporting youth sports, community health and player safety. item.title: How many points A’ja Wilson needs in 2027 to break into WNBA all-time top-10 scoring list
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Since being drafted as the first overall pick by the Las Vegas Aces in 2018, A’ja Wilson has cemented herself as one of the greatest players in the league’s history. The Aces came up short in the WNBA playoffs in 2026 but it was still a fantastic personal campaign for Wilson. She ended the regular season with the highest average across the league (26.2) ahead of Kelsey Mitchell (24.7) and Caitlin Clark (22.3). A’ja was similarly impressive in the postseason (27.5 average) and was also named the WNBA MVP for a record fifth time earlier this year. Now, while the 2027 campaign won’t begin for a while, she is almost certainly going to cement her name in the history books during it. As per Basketball Reference , the Aces star currently has 6,792 total career points in the WNBA. That puts her 11th in the all-time scoring list. However, she could break into the top 10 after just one game, as Wilson is only 11 points behind the now-retired Sue Bird, who occupies 10th place with 6,803 points. As well as Bird, A’ja could surpass 9th-place Cappie Pondexter (6,811) but may face a more difficult task when it comes to overtaking 8th. That position is held by Breanna Stewart (6,860), who is still active and will be competing with Wilson in the coming season. Meanwhile, though A’ja is a prolific points scorer, she is still some way off ever reaching the WNBA’s all-time points scorer, Diana Taurasi (10,646). item.title: AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership
item.description: Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can When you walk up from Haydons Road train station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium. AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter City – but that makes running a loss-making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board (DTB), which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.” Continue reading...

item.description: De la Fuente tells Tuchel ‘we’re not racists, none of us’ Tuchel hits out at media for ‘creating confusion’ Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in Spain after the England coach’s admission that he would remind his players of the anti-racism protocol prior to their meeting at the Metropolitano on Sunday night. This will be the first time the countries play each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse in a match at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004 . And although England have returned to Spain three times without incident since then, twice in Seville and once in Alicante, Tuchel was asked on Friday about going back in the buildup to Sunday’s game. The England coach replied that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” but also said: “Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid].” Continue reading...

item.title: De la Fuente feels the strain as Lamine Yamal club v country debate rages in Spain
item.description: Head coach hits out at ‘lies’ as suggestions of preferential treatment for young star overshadow preparations for England game in Madrid From the London Palladium to Madrid’s Metropolitano, they’re all here. On Sunday night, the footballers who lifted the game’s biggest awards meet again three weeks later and on the field this time, dinner jackets but not a single man left behind. Harry Kane, the Ballon d’Or and Gerd Müller trophy winner. Unai Simón, holder of the Lev Yashin award . Luis de la Fuente , the coach of the year who on Thursday night announced that also joining them will be Lamine Yamal , the kid who lifted the Kopa award as the best young player for the third year running and said he would have preferred Pau Cubarsí to be standing there instead. And, yes, Cubarsí will be there too for the final Nations League group game. At 1.45pm on Friday the world and European champions landed back at Madrid’s Barajas airport from Prague, where they had won again, before making their way by bus to their Las Rozas HQ, around the M40 motorway to the north-west of the capital. At about the same time, Lamine Yamal arrived from Barcelona, due in at midday. As was Mikel Oyarzabal , scorer of the winner at Euro 2024 and Spain’s top marksman this summer (not that he would ever tell you so) from San Sebastián. At 7.30pm, they trained, preparing to meet the World Cup semi-finalists and the team they defeated in Berlin at the end of Euro 2024. Two starters from the World Cup final will be absent: Dani Olmo and the captain, 2024 Ballon d’Or winner Rodri , are injured. But everyone else will be there. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. item.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football. The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United . That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
